$comment: Two things live here. `classes` is the fixed label order for every training run and for the manifest handed to Agent C (10 §6: index 0 = ped_walk, matching Detection.cls in 01 §7). `vlm_first_pass` is the strict output schema vlm_label.py sends to Claude Haiku 4.5 as output_config.format (10 §3.3). Boxes are normalized 0..1 in the 640x640 crop, YOLO convention (centre x, centre y, width, height). Nobody trains on an uncorrected VLM label.

class_definitions.ped_walk: The walking-figure lens is lit (steady). Box the lit lens face only, not the housing.
class_definitions.ped_hand: The hand lens is lit, steady or flashing, WITHOUT visible digits. Box the lit lens face.
class_definitions.ped_countdown: Digits are lit, with or without the hand. Box digits and hand together as one lens face.
class_definitions.none: No lens lit; lit vehicle signals; the head is out of frame; or the frame is an LED off-phase (skip it, do not label it as a negative when neighbouring frames show the lens lit).

label_every_head: Every lit pedestrian lens in the crop is labelled with its true class, including the perpendicular crosswalk's head. Rejecting the wrong head is the module's geometric gate (09 §5.1), measured end-to-end, never trained away.

x.description: box centre, fraction of crop width

y.description: box centre, fraction of crop height

unlit.description: true when no pedestrian lens is lit anywhere in the crop

perpendicularHeadVisible.description: a second pedestrian head, facing the cross street, is in the crop

offPhaseSuspected.description: a lens looks dark or banded in a way that suggests LED PWM / rolling shutter rather than a real unlit state

yolo_txt: One line per box: `<class_index> <x> <y> <w> <h>`, class_index from `classes`, coordinates normalized 0..1 in the 640x640 crop.
